g_policy.reason: The user opts in by choosing to play; the offer copy states the reward (3 Advanced reasoning answers today); 'Not now' leaves the chat unchanged; and the 'if the ad fails' field covers a game that is unavailable or unconfirmed.

g_no_cash.reason: The reward is 3 Advanced reasoning mode answers until midnight, which is an in-app usage allowance and has no cash value.

g_no_chat_content.reason: The trigger is opening the Teacher chat after a 3+ day gap with no session, which is an app event and needs no message content.

g_no_free_removal.reason: 'removes nothing free: yes'. Nothing free is capped or locked, because the reward is a sample of a paid feature.

g_brand_safety.reason: The placement is 'Inside the Teacher chat, right under Luzia's last reply', which puts the card in the message list. The reward-end 'small note in the chat' is also dressed up as a chat or system note.

c1_revealed_value.reason: For an existing_anchor, the app charges for Advanced reasoning mode. It is a paywall bullet (s02.e03, l02) in the Luzia+ plans.

c2_evidence.reason: Claims about today's app rest on s02.e03 (Advanced reasoning mode is a paid feature), s01.e02 (upsell badge) and s02.e19 (3-day trial). The rest is the proposal's own new card, copy and predictions.

c3_spares_payers.reason: The 'subscribers' field says members never see the card, and the Luzia+ plan shown does not remove ads, so paying users are spared.

c4_protects_subscription.reason: The reward is 3 answers that expire at midnight local time, which is a sample that ends. It takes nothing from other users or creators.

c5_moment.reason: The card appears when the user opens the chat after a gap, before any task is under way. It therefore doesn't interrupt an in-progress task.

c6_fits_simula.reason: It is a play-to-earn sponsored game. The reward is granted after a confirmed play (the failure path says 'If the play isn't confirmed...'), and the trigger is a detectable chat-open event.

c7_specific.reason: It names the Teacher chat (s07), the Luzia+ paywall's 'Advanced reasoning mode' bullet, the home badge and the 3-day trial button, so it is specific to this app.

other_concern: The proposal never shows how a free user switches on Advanced reasoning mode inside a chat; that interaction is unobserved. The rationale's claim that each answer 'pays for itself' in higher-earning markets is an unverified prediction.
